subject: Dedicated capacity launch: provisioning checklist & region decision

Subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding - kickoff and regional preference

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the intro — we’re excited to get Dedicated up and running. A few quick context items from our side:
- We plan to migrate two internal inference services (clinical summarization + triage classifier) to a dedicated GPU pool.
- Target go-live: mid-Jan 2027 (non-negotiable for Q1 roadmap).
- Expected steady throughput: ~6k tokens/s, burst to 20k tokens/s during morning windows.

Questions for the kickoff:
1) Are there recommended default regions for Priority Health (we are on AWS us-west-2, prefer minimize cross-region egress)?
2) What autoscale/burst recommendations do you typically start with for this profile?
3) Can you share a provisioning checklist we can review with our infra and procurement teams?

Attaching a short workbook with expected daily traffic and some token-level estimates.

Thanks — can we schedule a 30-min technical kickoff next week? Any of Mon/Tue morning PT works for us.

— Alicia

Hi Alicia — and thanks for the clear context, this helps a lot.

Quick answers up front:
- Region: us-west-2 is the sensible default given your AWS footprint; we'll avoid cross-region egress by colocating the pool in us-west-2. If you need multi-region failover we can discuss a passive standby in us-east-1.
- Autoscale baseline: for your steady 6k t/s we recommend a reserved pool sized for 8–10k t/s (buffer for model context and overhead) with burst capacity enabled up to ~25k t/s via short-term preemption slots.
- Checklist: attaching our Dedicated Provisioning checklist (provider-side tasks + customer gating items).

I'll loop in Monica for the implementation tasks and Karthik on kernel/quantization guidance.

Can we propose Tue 24 Nov 09:30 PT for the 30-min tech kickoff? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a brief agenda.

Best,

Thanks all — great to meet briefly on the call. Follow-up notes and action items below (capturing items we discussed + owners).

Priority Health — Dedicated onboarding action log (initial):

- PH-002: Signed SOW / procurement (Owner: Priority Health procurement) — due 2026-12-10

- PH-005: Autoscale & burst policy decision (Owner: PH SRE + Redwood) — due 2026-12-01

Notes/Recommendations:
- Recommended starting config: 6 x A100-equivalent instances with continuous batching config tuned for 2k token latency SLOs. This gives ~9–10k t/s steady depending on model choice; we’ll map exact numbers to your models during onboarding.
- Burst policy: suggest a two-tier policy — immediate short bursts (1–3 min) up to 3x baseline using preemptible capacity, and a secondary burst window (15–30 min) that uses reserved burst credits we keep pooled for you.
- Billing for burst: bursts are metered separately and will be outlined in the SOW (we can cap monthly burst spend if you want a hard guardrail).

Attachments: us-west-capacity-estimates.pdf (provisioning capacity table)

A quick technical note on autoscaling and kernel/quantization tradeoffs (per action PH-004):

1) Autoscale knobs we use:
   - scale_up_latency_threshold: 150ms p95 for small requests (short sequences)
   - scale_down_cooldown: 3m to avoid thrash during morning bursts
   - preemptible_fallback_ratio: up to 0.6 (i.e., 60% of burst capacity can be preemptible)

2) Burst sizing approach:
   - small bursts (<3m): route to preemptible instances with continuous batching; no model changes required
   - sustained bursts (>10m): use reserved burst credits and, where safe, switch to quantized variants (int8/4-bit) to increase throughput by ~1.8–2.5x depending on model.

3) Regional considerations:
   - us-west-2 has adequate GPU spot capacity historically; if your SLO requires guaranteed burst we should reserve explicit burst capacity in the SOW (we can price it separately).

4) Operational hooks:
   - We’ll provision a per-route cost threshold alert and an autoscaler-saturation alert for your SRE team.
   - For the first two weeks after cutover we recommend a read-only diagnostic feed to your team and a daily standby war room for 30m.

If you can share the model names and tokenization characteristics by EOD Mon (2026-11-30) I’ll produce a sizing sheet that maps to exact instance counts and quantization options.

— Rishi
